findings.title: Signal-killed git subprocess misreported as exit code 0
findings.detail: spawnCapture's close handler used code ?? 0, treating signal-killed processes (SIGKILL, SIGTERM) as exit code 0. git operations killed by the OS (OOM, timeout) silently appeared to succeed, allowing subsequent operations to proceed on an inconsistent repository state.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed to: code !== null ? code : signal ? 128 : 1. Signal kills now map to exit code 128, consistent with shell conventions.

findings.title: Corrupt verdict row throws unhandled exception crashing all PR decision reads
findings.detail: getAllPrDecisions and getPrDecisionsByRepo used .map() with a throw inside when encountering an unknown verdict string. Any single corrupt DB row caused the entire method to throw, making all PR decision reads fail for all callers until the row was manually removed.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed .map() to .flatMap() that logs and skips bad rows: corrupt rows are silently excluded with a console.error rather than crashing the entire read.

findings.title: Auto-router cache success path bypasses CACHE_MAX_SIZE eviction
findings.detail: The in-memory classification cache used cache.set() directly on the success path, bypassing the cacheSet() helper that enforces CACHE_MAX_SIZE=1000. The error path correctly used cacheSet(). Under sustained load the cache could grow without bound, exhausting heap memory.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed success-path cache.set() to cacheSet() so both paths enforce the 1000-entry cap with oldest-first eviction.

findings.title: markCapabilityBlocked leaves ifleet:in_progress label permanently stuck on blocked issues
findings.detail: GitHubQueue.markCapabilityBlocked() removed LABEL_IN_FLIGHT but not LABEL_IFLEET_IN_PROGRESS. Blocked issues showed the in-progress label indefinitely, misleading operators into thinking the task was actively running.
findings.fix_sketch: Added await this.removeLabel(task, LABEL_IFLEET_IN_PROGRESS) after the existing LABEL_IN_FLIGHT removal.

findings.title: watchForNew re-fires callback for terminal FAILED issues that also carry auto:ship label
findings.detail: GitHubQueue.watchForNew() filtered issues by the auto:ship label but did not exclude issues also carrying LABEL_FAILED. A failed issue with auto:ship would trigger the new-task callback on every poll cycle, causing spurious re-dispatch attempts.
findings.fix_sketch: Added guard: if (task.labels.includes(LABEL_FAILED)) continue; before firing the callback.

findings.title: CapabilityBridge leaks cancelled tasks indefinitely in taskMap
findings.detail: CapabilityBridge subscribed to task.completed and task.failed to clean up its taskMap but had no listener for task.cancelled. Tasks cancelled mid-flight remained in the map forever, creating a slow memory leak proportional to cancellation rate.
findings.fix_sketch: Added source.on('task.cancelled', (event) => { if (event.taskId) this.taskMap.delete(event.taskId); }) alongside the existing completed/failed listeners.

findings.title: allocateWorktree missing baseBranch validation — argument injection into git worktree add
findings.detail: allocateWorktree validated taskId against a strict regex but did not validate the baseBranch parameter. A caller with control over baseBranch could inject git flag-like strings (e.g. --orphan, -b something) into the git worktree add command.
findings.fix_sketch: Added: if (baseBranch !== undefined && !/^[a-zA-Z0-9._\-\/]+$/.test(baseBranch)) throw new Error(...) before the git call.

findings.title: Discord-source tasks without approvalGate throw confusing IssueCommenter invariant on HITL wait
findings.detail: runArchitect() would call issues.waitForApproval() for Discord-source tasks (issueNumber=0) that had autonomy=review but no approvalGate. Since no issues.comment() was called for issueNumber=0, the IssueCommenter threw 'waitForApproval called before comment() — no plan comment to poll for reactions', which is technically correct but obscures the real issue.
findings.fix_sketch: Added early return { attempt, plan, approved: false } for issueNumber <= 0 before the issues.waitForApproval() call, with a comment explaining Discord-source tasks require approvalGate.

findings.title: run command missing repo field length cap — inconsistent with sprint_goal validation
findings.detail: parseCommand's sprint_goal branch capped repo at 256 chars but the run branch had no cap. An attacker with a valid HMAC secret could submit an unbounded repo string via run.
findings.fix_sketch: Added if (parsed.repo.length > 256) throw new Error('run: repo exceeds maximum length') in the run branch, matching sprint_goal.

findings.title: Redundant removeEventListener calls in sleepOrAbort — once:true already auto-removes
findings.detail: sleepOrAbort added the abort listener with { once: true } which auto-removes it after the first fire. The timer callback and onAbort both also called signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort) redundantly. While harmless, it created confusion about whether the listener was being removed explicitly or implicitly.
findings.fix_sketch: Removed the explicit removeEventListener calls from both the timer callback and onAbort — relying solely on { once: true }.

findings.title: buildReviewerBrief includes user-supplied brief without content delimiter
findings.detail: The brief field (user-supplied GitHub issue body) was interpolated directly into the reviewer prompt under ## Original brief with no structural delimiter. A crafted brief could attempt to inject instructions into the reviewer's instruction layer.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrapped the brief in <user_supplied_content>...</user_supplied_content> XML tags to structurally separate it from the prompt instruction layer.

findings.title: rowToTask unchecked state cast can silently corrupt TaskState on DB schema drift
findings.detail: rowToTask cast row.state as TaskState without validation. If a future DB migration or manual edit introduced an unknown state string, the cast would silently produce an invalid TaskState value that downstream code (state machine guards, filters) would not handle correctly.
findings.fix_sketch: Added inline validation against the known state set ('pending','in_flight','done','failed','blocked'). Unknown states log a console.warn and fall back to 'failed' rather than silently trusting the cast.

findings.title: sumTokens conflates genuine zero token count with missing data
findings.detail: sumTokens returned undefined when the total was 0, treating both 'workers ran and used exactly 0 tokens' and 'workers reported no token data' as the same case. The JSDoc comment described the correct intent (undefined means missing data), but the implementation used total > 0 ? total : undefined which maps zero to undefined incorrectly.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed to check attempts.some(a => a.totalTokens !== undefined). Returns undefined only when no attempt surfaced token data; returns 0 when data exists but genuinely sums to zero.

findings.title: TaskStore.list() missing pagination offset — always returns from row 0 regardless of cursor
findings.detail: The list() method accepts a limit parameter but has no offset/cursor support. Callers implementing pagination call list() with increasing offsets but since the query ignores offset, every call returns from the beginning. On deployments with thousands of tasks, list() always returns the same first N rows.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an offset parameter (default 0) threaded into the SQL query as LIMIT @limit OFFSET @offset. Deferred: requires callers to be updated and integration tests added.

findings.title: listForIssueComment not paginated — HITL approval invisible beyond 100th reaction
findings.detail: waitForApproval uses octokit.reactions.listForIssueComment() which returns at most 100 reactions per call with no pagination. On a high-traffic issue with many reactions, approvals beyond position 100 are never seen. The poll loop can wait indefinitely for an approval that already exists.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace with octokit.paginate(octokit.reactions.listForIssueComment, {...}) to fetch all reaction pages before checking for approval. Deferred: requires testing the paginate call under the existing poll loop structure.
